structure: repos/trade-imports-reference-data at 9f3aa3e: a small Spring Boot (Java) REST service with no database repository. Read: docs/repos/trade-imports-reference-data.md, doc/adr/0002 (the only ruling; there is no decisions ledger), src/main/java/.../countries (CountriesController, Country, SubDivision), .../portsofentry (PortsOfEntryController, PortOfEntry), .../client (MdmClient Feign client, MdmService with caching and filtering, Mdm* payload classes), .../configuration/CacheConfig.java, src/main/resources/application.yml and the CountriesControllerIT integration test. The service exposes exactly two lists today: countries (with subdivisions) and ports of entry. Searching src/main for commodity, species, transporter, certification and document-type code found nothing, so every other list the scope names is recorded as a gap. Left out: metrics, logging, TLS, proxy and Mongo configuration, which are operational plumbing a journey page cannot observe.

claims.statement: The service serves a list of countries at GET /countries, each with a code, a name and a list of subdivisions.
Countries are returned sorted by name, ascending.
A country's code is the MDM effective alpha-2 code and its name is the MDM effective alias, not the long name.
Great Britain (code GB) is never returned in the countries list.
claims.note: The integration test also asserts that GB-NIR is absent from the response (CountriesControllerIT.java:45-46).

claims.statement: GET /countries takes an optional blocks query parameter. When given, only countries that belong to a block of that name with includeCountry true are returned; when absent, all countries (bar GB) are returned.
claims.note: A country whose MDM record has no blocks at all passes the filter even when a block is requested.

claims.statement: Each country carries its subdivisions as code and name pairs (for example Canary Islands, ES-CN). A subdivision with no code value is dropped, and a country with no subdivisions has an empty list.
The service serves a list of ports of entry at GET /ports-of-entry, each with a code and a name, sorted by name ascending.
claims.note: Only code and name are exposed; the MDM id is dropped.

claims.statement: Ports of entry come from MDM's border control post endpoint, and countries from MDM's geo countries endpoint, both called with the subscription key header and system=GBNAG. This service holds no reference data of its own.
MDM responses are cached in memory for CACHE_MDM_TTL_MINUTES (default 60). Empty results are never cached, and countries are cached separately for each distinct blocks value.
claims.note: CacheConfig.java:30-31 comments that the purpose is to rate-limit calls to MDM, not to defend against MDM unavailability.

claims.statement: If MDM returns no body for a countries or ports request, the service returns an empty list rather than an error.
claims.quote:
log.warn("MDM returned a null body for ports-of-entry request");
      return List.of();

claims.statement: The service has no inbound authentication of its own callers, and no notification, address or user data.
claims.quote: Authentication of its own callers: no inbound auth was found in the controllers.
claims.note: Inferred from the controllers carrying no security annotations; absence of auth was not proven by a test.

claims.statement: Ruling ADR 0002 (accepted 2026-05-07): trade-imports-reference-data is the shared home for several reference-data domains until one grows large enough to extract. Countries is the only domain it lists as currently managed; commodity codes and BCPs/POEs are listed as planned future domains to be added to this service first.
claims.quote: We will use `trade-imports-reference-data` as a shared service to manage multiple reference data domains until any individual domain grows large enough to justify extraction into its own dedicated service.
claims.note: The ADR is out of date against the code: it lists BCPs/POEs as planned, but GET /ports-of-entry is already implemented.
